changes.headline: Aramco headquarters struck in Dhahran; Hormuz takes two more ships
changes.dek: Aramco HQ administrative tower struck late Tuesday (limited fire, no casualties, production unaffected, staff home Wednesday); debris wounded 4 in Riyadh, 15 homes damaged; coalition strikes in Yemen; Riyadh airport closed to Oct 17; UKMTO: container ship and tanker struck Tuesday in Hormuz (26 ship strikes since Sep 29); Iranian officials tell Reuters tactics changed about 10 days ago; overnight tape WTI Nov26 $94.62 (+$0.48) / Brent Dec26 $106.35 (+$0.66). Late Tuesday a ballistic missile struck an office tower at Saudi Aramco's headquarters complex in Dhahran, damaging its top three floors (company source to Reuters). Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said an Aramco administrative building was attacked late Tuesday, causing a limited fire with no casualties, and petroleum production was unaffected; Aramco employees were instructed to work from home Wednesday. Debris from two intercepted Houthi cruise missiles wounded four people in Riyadh and damaged 15 homes. The Saudi-led coalition intercepted missiles and drones over Riyadh, the south and the Eastern Province on Tuesday and carried out airstrikes on Houthi sites in Yemen, including around an oil facility near Sanaa. Riyadh's King Khalid airport remains closed until Oct 17. In the Strait, UKMTO said a container ship and a tanker were struck by unknown projectiles on Tuesday; TradeWinds counts 26 ship strikes in the region since Sep 29. Two senior Iranian officials told Reuters Iran began using different offensive tactics about 10 days ago against vessels it considers in violation of its restrictions. Tuesday's settles split: WTI Nov26 about $94.14 (+0.4%), Brent Dec26 about $105.69 (-0.9%); overnight both are bid.
changes.balance_read: The premium is for a target list, not lost barrels: the only Saudi facility hit is administrative, production is untouched, and the overnight gain is under a dollar. Bulls hold an admitted Hormuz tactics change, a rising strike count, and a coalition now bombing fuel infrastructure in Yemen. Bears hold zero confirmed supply loss, Brent's Tuesday decline, and a fast Isaias restart. What would change the read is a hit on process or export assets, not another office building.
changes.publishers: Reuters, Oct 14, 2026; UKMTO via Reuters, Oct 13, 2026; TradeWinds, Oct 13, 2026; in-house quotes pull, Oct 14, 2026, 01:52 MDT

changes.headline: Diesel crack extends to $112.27, eighth day above $100; first clean day on energy targets
changes.dek: Diesel crack $112.27 (eighth straight day above $100, not a record; max $117.92 Sep 16); Russia reported no strikes on Ukrainian energy targets Tuesday, a first since Sunday's announcement; Moscow says the diesel deal is unlinked to peace talks; still no Russian diesel loading. The diesel crack reads $112.27 on the latest validated bar (history refreshed Oct 14): the eighth consecutive day above $100 (36 total days; all-time max $117.92, Sep 16). The 3-2-1 reads $62.14 (max $75.31, Aug 28). Russia's defence ministry summary for Tuesday made no mention of Ukrainian energy facilities, and no energy targets were reported hit overnight into Tuesday, after six energy sites were struck Monday; strikes on transport, logistics and residential targets continued. Zelenskiy said Tuesday Ukraine has not hit Russian refineries for two days. Russia's government said Tuesday it sees no direct link between peace talks and its diesel export deal with the US. No loading has been reported; the licence names no volumes or buyers, the 2022 statutory import ban objection stands, and Moscow's own export ban runs through October.
changes.balance_read: One clean day on energy targets is a data point, not a truce: no terms, no Russian confirmation, and heavy strikes on everything else. The crack extended anyway, which says the diesel market is pricing stocks (a record seasonal low) over talk. The first loading remains the break point; a second and third clean day on energy targets would be the ceasefire's first real evidence.
changes.publishers: Validated crack history, refreshed Oct 14, 2026; AAP/Reuters, Oct 13, 2026; Reuters, Oct 14, 2026

changes.headline: Canada trades again: Dec WCS -$25.55, C5 December down $1.00
changes.dek: TMW Dec26 -$25.55 (ICE, Oct 13; +$0.05, 780 lots), Nov26 -$24.85; ARV-TMW Dec +$8.95; TMS Nov26 +$7.02 (+$0.55); TMF Dec26 +$5.00 (down $1.00, 200 lots), Jan-Mar27 C5 down $1.00 to $1.30; EIA (w/e Oct 9) and IEA monthly both land today. Canadian diffs (ICE, Oct 13): TMW Nov26 -$24.85 and Dec26 -$25.55, still the widest tenor, on 780 December lots; ARV Dec26 -$16.60; ARV-TMW December +$8.95, the implied export arb, steady. SYN Nov26 +$7.02 (+$0.55) with Jan-Mar27 up $0.30 to $0.35, firming ahead of the Syncrude coker return wrapping Oct 16. C5 Dec26 +$5.00, down $1.00 on 200 lots, with Jan27 down $1.00, Feb27 down $1.00 and Mar27 down $1.30, a front-quarter condensate repricing. MSW Nov26 -$0.96 (+$0.27); UHC Dec26 +$2.35 (+$0.30). Isaias restart: the latest MMA update available remains Monday's, oil shut-ins 29.63% (604,503 b/d), down from 71.5% Friday. AESO Oct 14, 01:39 MDT: all monitored SAGD cogen units at full maximum capability. Today: EIA for the week ending Oct 9 (the Isaias week) and the IEA monthly report (10:00 Paris); no wire summary of the IEA report was available at assembly.
changes.balance_read: Heavy did nothing on a full session (December WCS a nickel firmer on real volume), which under extreme freight is the expected print. The information was in the lights: SYN firming into a supply return that has not landed, and C5 marked down a dollar across the front quarter. The November apportionment notice (about Oct 19) remains the next real heavy observation.

flags.title: Dhahran strike: target list escalated, supply count unchanged
flags.detail: An Aramco HQ administrative tower was struck late Tuesday: limited fire, no casualties, production unaffected, staff working from home Wednesday. The coalition is striking Houthi fuel infrastructure in Yemen and Riyadh airport is closed to Oct 17. The risk is the next rung of the target list, not barrels lost so far. Trigger: A strike hits Saudi process, pipeline or export assets, or Aramco reports any production or export impact

flags.title: Ceasefire: first clean day on energy targets; loadings still zero
flags.detail: Russia reported no strikes on Ukrainian energy targets on Tuesday, the first day since Sunday's announcement, after six energy sites were hit Monday. No terms, no Russian confirmation, and no Russian diesel cargo has loaded. The crack is eight days above $100 at $112.27. Trigger: A Russian diesel cargo loads, or a second and third consecutive day with no energy-target strikes

flags.title: SPR 40 Mbbl award still pending, eight days after bids
flags.detail: No DOE award announcement as of early Wednesday, eight days after the Oct 6 bid deadline. The award prices 40 Mbbl of medium sour into the Gulf for Nov-Dec delivery when it lands. Trigger: DOE announces the exchange award

forward_calendar.what: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report (w/e Oct 9) and IEA monthly report
forward_calendar.detail: First EIA weekly print with the Isaias shut-in week in it (Gulf shut-ins peaked at 71.5% Friday, down to 29.63% Monday on the latest MMA update available); the PADD 2 detail arbitrates the remaining Whiting question. The production line is a storm print, not current supply. IEA monthly lands the same day (10:00 Paris), one day after OPEC cut 2026 demand growth to 400 kb/d.

Bids went in Oct 6 (11:00 a.m. CT); a clean award prices 40 Mbbl of medium sour into the Gulf for Nov-Dec delivery. No award announced eight days later. Separately, DOE authorized a 4 Mbbl emergency SPR exchange Oct 10 (2 Mbbl each to ExxonMobil, BP America) for Isaias disruptions.

Syncrude's roughly 50-day coker turnaround window closes; SCO supply returns into late October, softening SYN against WCS. Suncor Edmonton/Base Plant fall work ended Oct 13 and the Horizon upgrader turnaround implies completion about Oct 12 to 13. SYN Nov26 firmed to +$7.02 on Oct 13, ahead of the return.

forward_calendar.what: Riyadh King Khalid airport closure scheduled to end
forward_calendar.detail: GACA has closed the airport to 21:00 GMT Oct 17 after the Houthi strikes. Whether it reopens on schedule is a read on Saudi air-defence confidence after the Dhahran Aramco HQ strike.
Decides whether the binding-from-November base case is right; December TMW is already pricing the seasonal wide (-$25.55, ICE settle Oct 13).
Next scheduled OPEC+ meeting; quotas are not the constraint, actual supply is.
